utterances.text: I merely know that they came, and they came on the paved Prizren-Gjakova road, with tanks and staff cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've gone a little ahead of where I'm directing your attention, sir. I'll just wait for translation. What I'm asking you now is: You said that there was a clash between the soldiers and the villager. Do you have any personal knowledge of what happened during that clash or the result of that clash?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: I know that the people left -- the residents left the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention very pointedly. What happened to those four soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Three were killed on the spot. One could leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the villager?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: He was killed on the spot too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these dead individuals personally or did you only hear about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: I only heard about them. I didn't see them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move on, then. About what time of the day had that clash occurred, to the best of your understanding?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: It was around 10.00. I am not very accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that clash where three of the four soldiers were killed, did something further happen in respect of your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: The troops came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon afterwards, do you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: After an hour. At 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say troops arrived. Can you describe to the Court, if you would, in as much detail as possible, what you mean by "troops"?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They came by tanks, Pragas, militia and army troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you had served in the JNA as a young man. Were you able to recognise or are you able to recognise uniforms, for example?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to describe what you mean by "tanks" and "Pragas"?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I would invite that the witness now be shown -- I believe it's Exhibit 18, first, if I may. Actually, before that's up, I should ask a couple of questions. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, to the best of your descriptive powers, tell the Court what these uniforms looked like on the soldiers you say were regular troops? What colour were they? What do they look like?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Army soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And army soldiers wear a particular kind of uniform, do they?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: The usual army uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the colour of what you understand to be a regular army uniform?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you try for us now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: There is nothing special. It's quite clear for everyone what an army uniform is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to describe it for us in words or would you only be able to describe it by recognition if you were to see a photograph of something like that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, I know the uniform. I can show it also if I see a photo or by words, as you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Try the words first, and then I'll show you a photo.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Regular army soldiers dressed in their uniforms. I saw the tanks, the usual tanks. That was how I saw it -- them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown what has been marked, I believe, in these proceedings as Exhibit number 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, sir, we're going to put that up on that ELMO, we call it. It's an overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: That's what I want to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's a particular photograph being shown on the ELMO. Did you ask the clerk to put that one up? Did you select that? I don't understand how it is that number 9 is on the ELMO. Was that at your request, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Let me see it. Let me have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Just for the record, Exhibit 18 has a number of photographs, each of which has a number in the top left-hand corner from 1 to 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us whether or not the regular army uniform to which you refer is shown on any of these numbered photographs on Exhibit 18, and if so, which one? Or more than one? Or any at all?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: This is not the one that I have in mind. I'm looking for something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the uniforms that you saw do not appear to you to be on this photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, you -- so you say you saw regular army uniforms. Did you see any other kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yeah. I saw the regular army uniforms myself, with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: No, nothing other than those regular army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, you've also told us -- I believe you used the word "tanks." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw. How many tanks, how many other vehicles did you see?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: I saw three tanks. One was bigger, two were smaller. And Pinzgauer and Pragas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Perhaps -- might the witness be shown the bundle of photographs in Exhibit number 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you're being handed by the clerk four sets -- four pieces of paper with some numbers on them. There are some vehicles depicted in those photographs, and each of those photographs has a number immediately under it.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the tank, the Praga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told us -- let's take this one at a time. You say you saw one large tank and two smaller tanks. Do you see a vehicle --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that looks like the bigger tank anywhere in these photographs or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the larger tank, and this is the Praga here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just take them one at a time. Sir, you've located what you call the larger tank. Does the photo you're looking at have a number underneath it, and if so, what is that number?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Number 2 and 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Okay. Could that be shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. You've shown 2 and now 1.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you've also indicated what you called a Praga. Do you see the Praga in any of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you point out and give us the number of the vehicle that most resembles what you call a Praga?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Could that be shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this rather large vehicle in number 4, that is what you refer to when you say "Praga"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you, from your military experience, do you know the difference between a tank and an APC, or an Armoured Personnel Carrier? Do you know the difference between those two?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Repeat the question, please. I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware if there is a difference or -- of the difference, if there is one, between what is known as a tank and Armoured Personnel Carrier, usually referred to as an APC?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at numbers 5 and 6 for us, if you would, please. Can you tell us what those are?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Number 7 is a Pinzgauer, and number 6 is a large tank, and number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's number 5?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 6 and 5 are tanks. All right. And what was number 2? Was that a tank as well?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you also said number 1. Did you call that a tank as well?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: It seems like a tank. I don't think it's a tank. No, it's not a tank. This one here is a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, when you say "this one here," what number are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Five is a tank.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: I was wrong before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When were you wrong? What are you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: When I said about number 2 and number 1. In fact, it's 6 and 5; and 7, it's Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to have to back up for a moment, sir, just to clarify this point. Let's go back to when you saw what you called tanks approaching your village. I believe you originally said that you saw them as number 2 and number 1. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: No. I was wrong. It's not number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were to correct yourself then, sir, what would you say were the tanks you saw?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Six, 5, and number 7 is the Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 7 is a Pinzgauer; is that what you're saying? And number 4 was a Praga; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, the Praga.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I note the time, Your Honours. I don't think I'm going to be able to complete this witness before the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers would you say -- I'm sorry. How many people in uniform would you say you saw, along with three tanks and these other military vehicles that you've just pointed out for us?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Groups of soldiers, five, six, some three, some four, five, not more, in a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where were these - I'm going to call them military vehicles - where were they located in relation to your village? Were they in your village, on the outskirts of the village? Where?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Outside the village, on the asphalt road which goes from Prizren to Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away is that from the edge of your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: The asphalt road is on the edge of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, happened upon the arrival of these uniformed people and their vehicles?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They shelled the houses. A group of families was on the hill. They shot 13 people, ranging from 18 months old to 60 years old. Lots of them were children. Some were injured, some seriously, some lightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the shelling go on?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: From 11.00 to 3.00. Four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effect did the shelling have on the village itself, other than you told us about 13 villagers being killed? What happened to the houses?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: As I said, they fired at the houses too, not very heavy shelling, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see from where you were -- I take it -- were you at your home when this happened?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see what was happening, if anything, to houses in the outlying area of Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, I could see from my home. I could see them shelling the houses. They shelled even my own home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the houses that were struck by shells?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Some they were destroyed, some were still standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers not in vehicles near the top of the hill?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: No. They came by buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And once they arrived --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: The infantry troops came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They began to torch the houses, and killed a person, one person. Avdi Morina [as interpreted] was his name. And then they put his body in the home and set fire to the home. Only his head was left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this person a relative of yours? I'm only asking that because he appears to have the same last name.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: No, he was not. Yes, we have the same last name, but he's a Gypsy. He was a Gypsy, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we'll return to the people that were killed later on in your evidence, but --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These infantry troops that came, did they come during the time that the houses were being shelled by the tanks or did they come at some later time, or when?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: The troops came after the shelling stopped. They came at 3.00. And then they began to set fire to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that these infantry arrived by buses. Are you able to give the Court an estimate as to how many people arrived, how many soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. About 150. I can't be sure. I couldn't tell, because I was hiding myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to infantry, did you see any other groups of uniformed individuals?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. There were some militiamen and soldiers. I can't say there were paramilitary troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "militia," is that another name for another group, or does that mean soldiers or police, or what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Police. I mean police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they referred to as the MUP?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those MUP police there along with the infantry troops?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see who was doing what?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them setting fire to the houses, and then they began to come down the village. They killed Avdi Gashi [as interpreted] and set fire to his home, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we move on, sir, there's a question I want to clarify with you. When you say "they," are you talking only infantry, only police, both infantry and police, or who?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Together, all of them: the police and the army troops, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see both police and infantry soldiers setting fire to houses and killing people?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They didn't kill many, only three people, because the others left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to get back to that, and this is as good a time as any. When did the others leave?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They left because of the fear. I'm not clear. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When in time -- now, you've told us on the 26th of March, at about 10.00, the police arrived -- or I'm sorry, soldiers arrived. Did they leave then, did they leave during the shelling, did they leave after the shelling? When?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Before the shelling, some. Some remained behind. My family left five minutes before the shelling. My wife, my brother, and myself stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did your family leave?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Because the village began to be shelled and to be burned. That's why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you just told us that your family left about five minutes before the shelling. Were you involved in the decision --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, five minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just listen to my question. Were you personally involved in the decision for them to leave?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: My wife couldn't leave with them because she couldn't walk, so I told her to stay with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you instruct your family to leave or did they decide on their own?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: They decided to leave themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Because of the shelling. How could they stay there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "because of the shelling," had that already started when they left?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes. A little bit before the shelling started, I told you five minutes ago, they left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I don't want to belabour the point, but the shelling had not yet started when your family decided to leave. Were they afraid of what would occur, or did they -- what happened?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: My brother came. My family was in the cellar. My brother said, "You cannot stay in the cellar. Let's go out." He took his family and my family and went to the forest and to the mountain, and we stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you and your wife decided to stay because your wife couldn't walk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else stay with you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: My brother too. He came to get us with them, but the shelling began, so we couldn't leave. We stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay at your house, or did you stay near the house, or what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: We stayed at home, in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: Until the infantry came. When they came to a cousin of mine, they started burning further up, and we went out and we fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: We went to a stream above the house about 500, 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that location, were you able to see what went on?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA
utterances.text: There is a kind of -- there was a kind of bank, and we were able to hide ourselves, and we were able to see from a distance houses being burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I note the time. I -- if this is a convenient place to break, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I have one thing to ask, a favour of Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Milosevic, yes, it's about the noise of the loudspeaker installed in front of you. At the outset of the trial, it seemed to the Court that you were not willing to use the headphone offered by the Tribunal, so we had the loudspeaker installed in front of you. During the trial, I noticed that you turned up the volume a little louder than was originally set, and I'm frankly a little bit disturbed by the noise. It's a little bit too loud. So could you turn it down a little lower, or why don't you use the headphones, as everybody else in the courtroom? Just bear it in mind for the next --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall bear that in mind. I've already suggested to the Registry that they put the loudspeaker behind me here. Then it will certainly be much quieter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Mr. Morina, we're not sitting tomorrow. The Court is not sitting. So we must ask you to come back, if you would, on Monday to conclude your evidence. Until then, would you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team, until it's over.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Half past nine, then, on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of February, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.05 p.m.,
